elements.element: Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence
elements.evidence: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence
professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000

elements.element: Cyber/privacy USD 5M where Vendor processes Customer Data
elements.evidence: cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering TrueLink's hosting of the Web Site and processing of Client Content and other Client data

elements.element: Workers' compensation as required by law
elements.evidence: workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law
shall provide Client with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request
errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000 (exceeds USD 1M)
cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 (exceeds USD 2M)

reasons: The inserted Section 31 satisfies every atomic element of the preferred position: CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M expressly tied to hosting and processing of Client data, statutory workers' compensation, and certificates upon request.

Insertion is appropriate because the Agreement contained no insurance covenant; the operation adds a new numbered clause and does not disturb the Force Majeure text or any other term, so intent is preserved and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced.

Minimality is slightly exceeded: the one-year post-term tail coverage requirement is an additional duration obligation not called for by the preferred position (which specifies coverages and certificates only). This is a low-severity drafting excess, not a substantive failure.
Fallback thresholds are comfortably exceeded, but the levels are assessed separately and the clause stands at the preferred level.
